results.summary: 1st Open Call round – Supporting SMEs in the Textile Sector towards Digital and Green Transition
results.content: 1st Open Call round – Supporting SMEs in the Textile Sector towards Digital and Green Transition

beneficiaryAdministration:
Applications must be submitted exclusively online via the Application Portal https://ec.europa.eu/eusurvey/runner/FutureProofTextiles-1st-OpenCall

  1. Technical Innovation (40%): Assesses the novelty, feasibility, and scalability of the proposed solution.
  2. Impact & Sustainability (30%): Evaluates the contribution to supply chain resilience, digitalization, and the green transition.
  3. Business Viability (20%): Measures market potential, financial sustainability, and commercialization strategy.
  4. Implementation Feasibility (10%): Reviews SME capacity, resource allocation, and the execution timeline outline.

Coordinated by UNIWA, a five-member international Evaluation Committee ensures a strictly confidential and impartial selection process, free from national or professional conflicts of interest. Applications are evaluated fairly against official criteria, with strict adherence to ESG standards and the EU’s "Do No Significant Harm" (DNSH) principle. Furthermore, selected projects must actively integrate climate-neutral, circular economy practices and strive for gender equality across all personnel levels.
description:
Link to the online Application Portal : https://ec.europa.eu/eusurvey/runner/FutureProofTextiles-1st-OpenCall

Open Call objective: Empowering 20 SMEs in the textile sector to successfully navigate the "twin transitions" of digital transformation and green sustainability.

Support: Beyond the €60,000 co-financing grant (50 000 EUR – fixed lump Sum Grant, 10 000 EUR – required self-funding by SME), FutureProofTextiles offers extensive capacity-building and networking resources to help build a connected SME ecosystem:

  1. Tailored Training: An average of 40 hours per SME focusing on digital transformation, circular economy principles, and sustainable production.
  2. Dedicated Mentoring: Custom technical consulting and mentoring sessions for up to 6 selected SMEs based on specific needs.
  3. Open-Access Materials: Production of 100 hours of scalable training curricula and best-practice guides for the broader textile sector.
  4. Cross-Border Networking: Facilitation of international collaboration to foster an innovative textile ecosystem.

(Further details regarding these services will be shared with the selected SMEs.)

Who can apply:

Company size

  1. Applicants must fall under the category of SME, according toEuropean Commission Recommendation 2003/361/EC*
  2. Partnerships Clusters and intermediary organisations are not eligible even if they are SMEs.
  3. Each applicant should represent a single SME, not a consortia of multiple SMEs.

Industry

  1. Applicants must be SMEs operating in the textile value chain. SMEs from complementary sectors (e.g., tech, machinery) are also eligible, provided their proposed innovation directly contributes to the textile value chain. Activities must align with a relevant NACE code (or national equivalent), such as:
  2. Textile manufacturing: C13.1, C13.2, C13.3, C13.9
  3. Apparel manufacturing: C14.1, C14.3
  4. Textile-based products and technical textiles: C15.12, C22.19
  5. Textile recycling and circularity: C38
  6. Digital and innovative solutions for the textile sector: J62, J63
  7. Manufacture of machinery for textile, apparel and leather production:C 28.94

Location

  1. Only SMEs legally established in countries participating in the Single Market Programme (SMP) are eligible to apply. This includes EU Member States and any other country formally associated with the SMP. A full list of participating countries is published here: List of participating countries in the Single Market Programme (SMP)

Language

  1. The applicant SME must have at least one staff member who speaks English and will be actively involved in the implementation process, handling all communication needs with the consortium.

Submission Rules:

Platform

  1. Proposal submitted online on the EU Survey Platform. Any other means will not be accepted. Application Form

Language

  1. Proposals must be written in English. Submissions done in any other language will not be evaluated.

Submission Limit

  1. Applicant SMEs may submit up to two proposals per Open Call round (one under Green Transition and one under Digital Innovations). Despite this, each SME is eligible to receive a maximum of one grant award across the entire program.

Proposal Requirements

  1. The proposal must demonstrate a Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of 5 or higher.

Compliance & Ethics

Applicants must confirm their full compliance with all rules, including absence of double funding, and conflict of interest, by reviewing and signing the mandatory forms included in the application:

  1. Funding eligibility and absence of conflict of interest declaration form
  2. SME and Eligibility declaration form

Step by Step Guide

Applicants may submit one proposal for a Green Transition project and one for a Digital Innovation project. Please note that a separate application must be submitted for each.

Step 1: Verify Eligibility

Review the eligibility requirements thoroughly to ensure your organization and project qualify for funding.

Step 2: Concept & Budgeting

  1. Check out “Exhaustive List of Eligible Activities and Eligible Costs” document.
  2. Check out “Needs of the SMEs in the Textile Sector” document, which helps the brainstorming process.
  3. Brainstorm your proposal. When brainstorming, keep in mind that the project implementation period is 9months.
  4. Compose an initial draft, and develop a comprehensive budget based on eligible costs. Clearly define your objectives by establishing specific milestones.

Step 3: Draft Responses

  1. Prepare your answers for each section of the “Standardized Application Form Template” document, before starting the online submission.

Step 4: Prepare Mandatory Documents

Complete and sign the following required forms:

  1. Complete the “Tables with Activities, Budget, Milestones, and Risks” document. Please note that milestones may be subject to negotiation if the proposal is selected, and applicants will not be evaluated based on the proposed milestones
  2. Fill in the “SME and Eligibility Declaration form”.
  3. Fill in the “Funding eligibility and absence of conflict of interest declaration form”.

Step 5: Complete the Online Form

Access the online portal – EU Survey to input your responses. We recommend using a stable internet connection to prevent data loss.

Step 6: Upload Attachments

Attach all mandatory documents from Step 4 into their respective upload fields within the form.

All necessary documents are available for downloading through the Application portal and through the relevant posts in projects LindeIn and ECCP page.

results.summary: Dual-Use Drones Innovative Programme
results.content: Dual-Use Drones Innovative Programme

beneficiaryAdministration:
Call amendment 18th of September 2026: The following sentence has been included in section 4.2: "If selected for funding, SMEs will be asked to set-up a PIC number."

The Dual-Use Drones Innovative Programme is a European initiative supporting SMEs that already belong to the dual-use market to develop drone projects that adapt their business models, processes and products to address civil, digital, social and environmental needs.

Objectives

The Programme aims to support SMEs in:

  1. the technological maturation of their drone solutions,
  2. the structuring of their innovation strategy,
  3. improvement and adaptation of their business models, processes and products to address civil, digital, social and environmental needs.

Support Offered

Selected SMEs will benefit from:

·Individual assessment and roadmap definition.

·     Mentorship throughout the Programme.

·Tailored technical, regulatory, business and testing services as explained in Annex 3.

·Access to training and internationalisation support.

·Possibility to participate in the Innovation Drone Alliance.

·      Equity-free funding of up to €35,000 per SME.

Some activities are mandatory, while others are optional depending on the SME’s needs.

Each selected SME will implement an Innovation Plan, which will serve as the main reference for participation in the Programme.

Submission Process

Applications must be submitted electronically via the Wiin.io online platform.

The deadline to apply is 30th of September 2026 at 5pm CEST

Application Form

Applicants must complete the online application form and upload all required information and mandatory supporting documents as specified on the submission platform.

Incomplete applications will be rejected.

Each SME may submit one application written in English only.

Applicants may be contacted for clarification during the evaluation process. Failure to respond within the specified timeframe may result in ineligibility of the application.

Evaluation and Selection

Eligible applications will be evaluated by independent experts based on the following criteria:

  1. Excellence and Innovation – 30 points
  2. Quality and Implementation – 40 points
  3. Impact – 30 points

To be considered for selection, applications must:

  1. achieve a minimum overall score of 50/100, and
  2. score at least 50% of the maximum points in each evaluation criterion.


Eligibility Conditions

Eligible applicants must be manufacturing SMEs operating in the drone sector that seek to upgrade their product technologically and to develop or strengthen Dual-use applications. They need to meet all of the following conditions:

·Be an SME according to EU rules (Recommendation 2003/361/EC[1]), which means:

oBe independent or compliant with EU definitions of autonomous partner or linked enterprises.

oEmploy fewer than 250 persons and

o  have an annual turnover ≤ €50 million, or an annual balance sheet total ≤ €43 million.

To ensure you have the correct status, Applicants are asked to fill in the SME self-assessment from the European Commission and upload the result on the Application Form.

·Have at least one drone product at TRL 6 or higher and commit to upgrading the TRL by at least one level during participation in the Programme (a proof of TRL will be required during the application process).

·      Be legal entities established and operating in:

o  An EU Member State, or

o  A country participating in the EU Single Market Programme/COSME Strand

·Submit a full application in English including all required proofs as detailed in Section 3.2 of the Guide for Applicants.

SMEs will remain eligible throughout the Programme even if they temporarily exceed SME financial thresholds during project implementation.

NOT eligible for the ECDI Dual-Use Innovative Programme are:

·      Applications focused solely on market access without product development

·      Companies such as: Software-only companies (including SaaS providers), Companies providing drone-based services or operations, Data processing, analytics, or AI companies without a proprietary drone-related hardware product, Consultancy, engineering, or training providers, Companies commercialising solutions based exclusively on third-party drone hardware, Companies that do not develop and manufacture a tangible drone-related product, component, subsystem, or infrastructure

·      SMEs without an eligible product (below TRL 6)

Eligibility Conditions Step 2:

Applicants must meet all legal, financial, and compliance requirements to be considered. Here summarized:

General eligibility conditions

  1. SME Status: Applicants must qualify as an SME according to the EU SME definition (Commission Recommendation 2003/361/EC). This covers headcount, turnover, and balance sheet totals, taking into account any linked enterprises.
  2. Geographical Eligibility: Organizations must be legally established in a Single Market Programme (SMP) participating country, including EU Member States and SMP associated countries.
  3. Financial Capacity: Applicants must demonstrate the financial viability to manage and sustain project activities, verified via an indicator-based assessment.
  4. Exclusion Criteria: Applicants must not be in any exclusion situations (e.g., bankruptcy, fraud, or corruption) as defined in Article 136 of the EU Financial Regulation.
  5. EU Compliance: Projects must adhere to standard EU obligations, including conflict of interest avoidance, confidentiality, data protection, DNSH (Do No Significant Harm) principle, compliance with the EU AI Act (where applicable), EU funding visibility and cooperation with checks/audits.

Step 2 specific requirements

  1. Project focus: proposals must build on a Step 1-selected idea, clearly focused on Cultural Heritage Value Chain (CHVC) and targeting one single strand (Strand 1 – Product Innovation or Strand 2 – Process Innovation). Check Step 1-selected ideas at the following rankings document: Step 1 Results.
  2. Participation limits: a single SME may participate as applicant in only one (1) proposal, whether as Lead Partner or as Project Partner.
  3. Consortium composition: projects must include at least two (2) applicant SMEs.
  4. Lead Partner: must be a Step 1-selected SME (check Step 1 Results), must have completed the mandatory Capacity Building and Matchmaking activities (May–June 2026), and must have filled the satisfaction questionnaire. Completion of the mandatory Capacity Building and Matchmaking sessions can be checked here: Attendance CBP.
  5. Mandatory deliverables: projects should include strand mandatory deliverables, and the participation to at least one European networking/business event.
  6. Application of EU-based technologies and/or engagement of Innovation Leaders: applicants must demonstrate that their project will apply EU-based digital solutions and/or technologies and/or engage EU-based Innovation Leaders.
  7. Financial requirements: the requested EU grant must correspond to the fixed strand grant amount (€120,000.00 for Strand 1 / €77,000.00 for Strand 2). Each single SME may request maximum €60,000.00, including linked enterprises. The EU Grant covers up to 85% of the total project budget; consortia must provide at least 15% co-financing.
  8. Applications must be written in English and submitted electronically through the following link by the set deadline.

For all the details on Step-2 specific requirements, check the Call document, Section 3.2, Step 2-specific submission requirements and procedure and Section 5.4, Step 2 Evaluation and selection criteria.


The Call offers financial support through two distinct strands:

  1. Strand 1 - Product Innovation: Directed at the development of new-to-the-firm products or services (Grant amount: €120,000.00 fixed lump sum for consortia of at least 2 SMEs).
  2. Strand 2 - Process Innovation: Directed at business process innovation linked to green and digital transition (Grant amount: €77,000.00 fixed lump sum for consortia of at least 2 SMEs).

The maximum amount that will be granted to each SME is € 60,000.00.


The submission procedure

Step 2 applications must be submitted by the Lead Partner electronically through the F6S Platform via the Call for Proposals page at the following link:

https://www.f6s.com/cultural-heritage-grants-step-2/apply

Deadline: 31 August 2026 at 17:00 (Brussels time)


Important: Selected projects of Step 1 are eligible to apply to Step 2. Results of Step 1 are available at the following link: Step 1 Results.


Detailed information about Step 2 can be found in the Call documents (full Call Package):

  1. Call for Proposals document
  2. Call annexes
description:
Applicant projects, that passed Step 1 evaluation (Results of Step 1 are available at the following link: Step 1 Results), are invited to submit proposals for collaborative innovation projects specifically focused on the Cultural Heritage Value Chain (CHVC). Projects must contribute to European strategic autonomy and the twin transition (green and digital).

The Call provides two distinct funding strands, both directly applied to the CHVC:

  1. Strand 1. Product Innovation
  2. Strand 2. Process Innovation

Proposals must build on a Step 1-selected idea, maintaining the previously selected strand.

For further information, please check the full Call Package.


Key Requirements:

  1. Consortium: The Step 2 proposal must be submitted by a consortium of at least two SMEs from eligible SMP countries. While Lead Partner must be a Step 1-selected SME, Project Partners may include SMEs not selected in Step 1, if they meet general eligibility. Associated Partners may be added without EU funding (their involvement does not count towards the minimum eligibility requirements of this Call).
  2. Technology: Projects must demonstrate the application of EU-based digital solutions/technologies (Option A) and/or the engagement of Innovation Leaders (Option B). Access the Innovation Leaders catalogue to browse the listed stakeholders. Innovation Leaders may be engaged as:
  3. an applicant SME within the consortium (if the Innovation Leader qualifies as an SME and meets all eligibility requirements of this Call).
  4. an external entity (either as an Associated Partner, or as a Service Provider)
  5. Duration: The project implementation period is fixed at 12 months.
  6. Co-financing requirement: the EU Grant covers up to 85% of the total project budget; therefore consortia must provide at least 15% co-financing. This contribution is mandatory for all participating SMEs within a project. The co-financing may be covered directly by SMEs' own resources or by external private funding. While 15% is the minimum requirement, providing a higher percentage of co-financing will result in additional points during the evaluation process.
  7. Other financial aspects: the financial support provided under this Call is a Grant structured as a lump sum, meaning that payments are linked to the achievement of project milestones and the approval of technical reports. While the grant will be managed according to a lump sum approach, in Step 2 the budget must be submitted based on real costs using the mandatory templates in Annex 5 or Annex 6, so that evaluators can assess how the project budget is structured, whether it is coherent with the proposed activities, and how the required co-financing will be covered. The costs included in the budget must be incurred in the project period, be connected with the action and necessary for its implementation, comply with applicable national laws, be reasonable and justified and comply with the principle of sound financial management. VAT is not eligible and therefore should not be included as an eligible cost.

Mandatory annexes to be submitted in Step 2: the following mandatory annexes must be submitted through the platform, in line with the application procedure described in the Call document. Call annexes are available at this link.

  1. Annex 4 - Step 2 Application Form: duly completed and signed by all applicants (the form includes a Declaration of Honour (DoH) that must be signed by the legal representative of each SME requesting funding).
  2. Annex 5 or Annex 6 - Step 2 Budget Template: Applicants should fill Annex 5 or 6 depending on the selected strand (Strand 1 or Strand 2).
  3. Financial viability self-assessment: completed using the self-assessment tool, printed and signed for each SME requesting funding. Follow the instructions provided in Annex 2.
  4. Proof of legal registration: for each SME requesting funding. E.g., company register extract, certificate of incorporation, or equivalent official registration document. Provide English translation where applicable (see the Call document).
  5. Balance sheet, and Profit and loss account for the last two closed financial years: for each SME requesting funding. Provide English translation where applicable (see the Call document).
  6. Mandatory questionnaire: mandatory questionnaire available at this link. Filled in by the Lead Partner and saved as a pdf document.

beneficiaryAdministration:
Submission: the application form and all supporting documents must be submitted in English, before the deadline, through the EU Survey platform at this link: https://ec.europa.eu/eusurvey/runner/PowerUpNetZero_Call_InnovationProjects

An email confirming the receipt of the application will be sent to the main contact person (who filled the application).

In order for the application to be considered eligible, all the following supporting documents must be filled in English, signed and uploaded in the application form before the deadline:

· Activities timeline, budget and KPIs: based on an excel file provided by PowerUp NetZero.

· Declaration of Honour: template provided by PowerUp NetZero, must be signed and dated.

· Result of the SME Financial Viability Self-Check - available at the following link: https://ec.europa.eu/research/participants/lfv/lfvSimulation.do

All documents are availanble at the following link: https://piemonteinnova.it/second-powerup-netzero-open-call-innovation-projects/

The evaluation process consists of:

1.Eligibility check (by 25th September 2026).

2.Evaluation process made by an Evaluation Panel which will evaluate and score the relevance, impact, and implementation sections of the application.

3.Once the evaluation process is completed, all applicants will receive an e-mail about the final results (deadline 19th October 2026).

4.Agreement signature (only for selected applications) with one of the PowerUp NetZero Open Call for Innovation Projects partner of reference (FPI or EnviPark) (deadline 13th November 2026).

Each beneficiary Consortia of this call can receive up to 120.000,00 EUR in the form of a lump-sum (thus, it is expected that at least 14 projects will receive financial support).

Beneficiaries can participate to the different PowerUp NetZero Open Calls (Business Innovation Services and Technology Adoption Activities or Innovation Projects) but a single beneficiary cannot receive more than 60.000,00 EUR overall.

Only one application per SME and Consortia will be accepted under this specific call.

If an entity submits more than one proposal, as a general rule, only the first proposal submitted will be considered eligible for evaluation.

Starting of projects: 16th November 2026, with a duration of maximum 10 months from the signature of the agreement.

The applications selected will be funded until the budget limit of the PowerUp NetZero Open Call for Innovation Projects is reached.

The PowerUp NetZero OPEN CALL FOR INNOVATION PROJECTS provides financial support for helping SMEs and start-ups adopt or improve net-zero technologies and solutions (Solar energy, Battery and energy storage, H2 technologies, Sustainable biogas and biomethane, Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS)) in their processes, products or services. The call for innovation projects targets companies working together to implement:

  1. PoC or testing of new / improved environmentally friendly products.
  2. Net-zero solutions and services.
  3. Pilot /demonstration actions.

A high degree of innovation is expected in response of this call. Funded activities could address technical risks associated with the demonstration of innovative technologies and solutions, such as optimising technology processes and operational parameters and/or improving the characteristics of their products/solutions. Innovation projects should demonstrate an innovative net-zero technology or solution in an operational or in a Virtual & Industrially Relevant environment (TRL 6-7) but are not necessarily expected yet to reach large scale demonstration or commercial production.

Applicants must be Consortia of minimum two (2) and maximum three (3) SMEs (also including start-ups provided they are SMEs) established in an EU Member State or in a country participating in the Single Market Programme (SMP) at the moment of the call launching date.

results.content: Net Zero Technology - Demo Projects Open Call #1

beneficiaryAdministration:
Applications are submitted online via the GoodGrant platform within the defined deadline. After submission, proposals undergo an eligibility check by the consortium and then an evaluation by independent experts based on predefined criteria (Excellence, Impact, Implementation). Proposals meeting the minimum thresholds are ranked, and funding is awarded to the highest-scoring projects until the available budget is exhausted. 10 projects will be funded.

The minimum consortium is 2 SMEs from 2 different eligible regions (NUTS 2).
description:
This Open Call supports SMEs, either as manufacturing end-users or solution providers, in implementing advanced processes and technologies that accelerate the transition towards net-zero manufacturing.

Proposals must address a concrete manufacturing use-case, demonstrating direct application within an industrial production environment.

Actions shall focus on the deployment and demonstration of mature, near-to-market solutions in real industrial environments (TRL 7–8). The objective is to bridge the gap between applied research and market uptake by enabling scalable, operational implementation.

Projects must :

  1. Deliver reductions in greenhouse gas emissions and environmental impact;
  2. Improve energy efficiency and/or optimize resource use;
  3. Integrate innovative and qualified digital technologies (e.g., IoT, AI etc.);
  4. Be clearly embedded in a manufacturing context and demonstrate measurable results.

Eligible activities. The following activities may be supported under this Open Call, provided they are directly linked to the objectives of the project and contribute to the demonstration and deployment of Net-Zero Technologies in a manufacturing context:

·Demonstration and pilot activities

  1. Deployment and testing of technologies in real or operational industrial environments
  2. Pilot lines, protoptypes, demonstrators, or proof-of-concept validation at TRL 6–8
  3. Integration of technologies into existing production systems

·Technology implementation and adaptation

  1. Customisation and integration of NZT solutions into manufacturing processes
  2. Retrofitting or upgrading industrial equipment to improve energy efficiency or reduce emissions
  3. Process optimisation and digitalisation (e.g. IoT, AI, data-driven monitoring)

·Digital solutions for sustainability

  1. Adopting or deployment of digital tools for energy monitoring, optimisation and management
  2. Consumption/resource reduction, tracking and valorisation systems
  3. Digital twins or predictive maintenance solutions improving resource efficiency

·Circular economy implementation

  1. Reuse, recycling or recovery of materials within production processes
  2. Development of circular production systems or industrial symbiosis approaches
  3. Reduction of raw material consumption and waste generation

·Testing, validation and performance assessment

  1. Measurement and verification of environmental impact (e.g. GHG emissions reduction)
  2. Life-cycle or performance assessments directly linked to the demonstration
  3. Validation of scalability and replicability of the solution
  4. Activities that fill the gap between demonstration and commercialization.

Applicants are most welcome to also include upskilling, and/or internationalization and value chain strengthening activities, and/or promotion activities, to show the scalability of the solution and contribute to Europe’s leadership in sustainable manufacturing.

Projects must clearly indicate :

  1. TRL before project start
  2. TRL expected at project completion

Projects should typically aim to progress from TRL 5–6 toward TRL 7-8.

callTitle: Net Zero Technology - Demo Projects Open Call #1
furtherInformation:
The call aims to :

• Accelerate the deployment of Net-Zero Technologies (NZT) in manufacturing

• Support the development of European NZT solutions

• Support trans-regional and trans-national SME collaboration

• Strengthen European industrial competitiveness.

• Contribute to industrial decarbonisation

Projects must address at least one of the following NZT categories :

• Battery and energy storage technologies : Technologies that improve energy retention, efficiency, and management (e.g., advanced battery cells, thermal storage, etc.)

• Hydrogen technologies : Specifically focusing on electrolysers (production of green hydrogen) and fuel cells (using hydrogen for power), which are critical for decarbonizing heavy industry and transport.

• Electricity grid technologies : Solutions that make the power grid smarter, more flexible, and capable of handling high loads of renewable energy.

Applications must be submitted electronically via the BIONetZero application platform.

Applicants are required to:

  1. create a user profile on the application platform,
  2. complete the online application form in English, and
  3. upload the required annexes (including a pitch deck).

Only complete applications submitted before the call deadline will be considered.

Applications will be evaluated by the BIONetZero Evaluation Committee with the support of external experts. Evaluation will be based on transparent criteria, including:

  1. relevance of the problem addressed,
  2. quality and innovation level of the biosolution,
  3. technological maturity and feasibility,
  4. market potential and scalability,
  5. capacity and commitment of the SME team,
  6. alignment with the objectives of the BIONetZero project.

Applicants will be informed of the evaluation outcome via the application platform and by email.

All applications are submitted under Financial Support to Third Parties (FSTP) rules in accordance with the Single Market Programme (SMP). SMEs may receive a maximum total of EUR 60,000 in financial support across all stages of the BIONetZero programme.

A co‑financing rate of 25% applies to all grants.
description:
Under this call, selected Small and Medium‑Sized Enterprises (SMEs) will participate in Stage 1 of the BIONetZero Acceleration Programme (Ideation & Travel Grant).

The objective of Stage 1 is to support SMEs in:

  1. refining and positioning their biosolution concept,
  2. strengthening their technical and commercial roadmap, and
  3. building relevant European and international networks.

Selected SMEs will be required to:

  1. participate in a mandatory BIONetZero kick‑off and networking event organised in Denmark,
  2. engage in structured networking, peer‑learning and knowledge‑exchange activities,
  3. work with a designated BIONetZero Key Account Manager (KAM) to shape a clear development pathway for their biosolution.

Stage 1 focuses on ideation, networking and preparation and does not include technology development activities.

Participation in Stage 1 is a mandatory prerequisite for applying for further financial support under the BIONetZero programme. However, acceptance into Stage 1 does not guarantee access to funding in subsequent stages.

The BIONetZero programme follows a four‑stage cascade funding model, with possible progression to:

  1. Stage 2: Tech Grant (TRL 4–6),
  2. Stage 3: Implementation Grant (TRL 7–8),
  3. Stage 4: Internationalisation Booster.

Progression between stages is subject to additional evaluation and selection.

results.summary: Civil Drones Innovative Programme
results.content: Civil Drones Innovative Programme

beneficiaryAdministration:
The Civil Drones Innovative Programme is a European initiative supporting SMEs developing innovative technologies for civil and dual-use drones, implemented under the European Cluster for Drone Innovation (ECDI) project.

Objectives

The Programme aims to support SMEs in:

  1. the technological maturation of their drone solutions,
  2. the structuring of their innovation strategy,
  3. access to civil and defence-related markets.

Support Offered

Selected SMEs will benefit from:

  1. individual assessment and roadmap definition,
  2. mentorship throughout the Programme,
  3. tailored technical, regulatory, business and testing services,
  4. access to training and internationalisation support,
  5. possibility to participate in the Innovation Drone Alliance,
  6. equity-free funding of up to €50,000, linked to the Innovation Plan.

Some activities are mandatory, while others are optional depending on the SME’s needs.

Each selected SME will implement an Innovation Plan, which will serve as the main reference for participation in the Programme.

Submission Process

Applications must be submitted electronically via the Online Platform.

The Open Call is organised in two cut-off dates.

Eligible applications not selected in the 1st cut-off and below the minimum threshold may:

  1. be resubmitted to the 2nd cut-off, provided that the application is updated and improved based on feedback received.

Eligible applications not selected in the 1st cut-off and above the minimum threshold may choose between:

  1. being placed on the reserve list and re-integrated in the assessment after the 2nd cut-off, or
  2. being resubmitted to the 2nd cut-off, provided that the application is updated and improved based on feedback received.

Application Form

Applicants must complete the online application form and upload all required information and mandatory supporting documents as specified on the submission platform.

Incomplete applications may be rejected.

Each SME may submit one application per cut-off date.

Applicants may be contacted for clarification during the evaluation process. Failure to respond within the specified timeframe may result in rejection.

Evaluation and Selection

Eligible applications will be evaluated by independent experts based on the following criteria:

  1. Excellence and Innovation – 30 points
  2. Impact – 30 points
  3. Quality and Implementation – 40 points

To be considered for selection, applications must:

  1. achieve a minimum overall score of 50/100, and
  2. score at least 50% of the maximum points in each evaluation criterion.

Applications will be ranked after each cut-off.

All applicants will be informed of the evaluation results.

Unsuccessful applicants will receive feedback.

Eligibility Conditions

Applicants must be manufacturing SMEs operating in the drone sector and seeking to upgrade their product technologically and develop or strengthen dual-use applications.

Applicants must:

  1. qualify as an SME under EU Recommendation 2003/361/EC,
  2. be independent or compliant with EU definitions of partner/linked enterprises,
  3. employ fewer than 250 persons and have:
  4. an annual turnover ≤ €50 million, or
  5. an annual balance sheet total ≤ €43 million,
  6. have at least one drone product at TRL 6 or higher and commit to increasing the TRL by at least one level during the Programme.

Applications focused solely on market access without product development are not eligible.

Service providers, non-manufacturing companies, or SMEs without an eligible product (below TRL 6) are not eligible.

Start-ups without full financial history may be eligible if SME criteria are met.

Applicants must not be bankrupt, under liquidation, considered an enterprise in difficulty, or subject to EU funding exclusion.

Applicants must complete the EU SME self-assessment and upload the result with their application.

Eligible Countries

Applicants must be established in:

  1. an EU Member State, or
  2. a country participating in the EU Single Market Programme / COSME Strand.

Number of SMEs to be Supported

The Programme aims to support around 25 SMEs:

  1. approximately 13 SMEs at the 1st cut-off,
  2. approximately 12 SMEs at the 2nd cut-off.

The consortium reserves the right not to award all available funds.

Further Information

  1. Guide for Applicants
  2. ECDI website
  3. ECDI LinkedIn

Contact: vidal@aerospace-valley.com and carbon@aerospace-valley.com

  3. Market launch preparation

  1. Development of new or significantly improved products
  2. Development of innovative services
  3. Preparation for market entry

Projects must demonstrate:

title: Agri-food Biotech Scaling-up
descriptionByte:
Expected Outcome:

Indicative duration of the project(s) to be funded: 36 months

Qualitative and quantitative indicators: The number of collaboration activities, the scale-up achieved by SMEs in terms of volume increase and/or measurable process improvements (e.g. higher yields, lower costs), and the number of SMEs supported overall.

Scope:

This call will fund projects within the bioeconomy, with a special focus on biotech applied in the food sector. The projects aim at boosting collaboration between biotech clusters, creating a critical mass able to compete with global hubs. Projects will have to actively support their SMEs developing innovative products made with bio solutions, especially to scale-up from the laboratory to pilot- and commercial scale, and explore the best options to provide regulatory support to help bring those products to the market.

Projects should focus on the agri-food sector, and the use of fermentation technologies (such as biomass fermentation and precision fermentation) which already contribute to food sustainability and security and will increasingly do so. Fermentation technologies present opportunities to offer diverse, nutritious and accessible food options with reduced use of land. They also present economic opportunities for rural areas, as biomass fermentation allows for rapid production of protein-rich foods with minimal inputs, adaptable to any location with access to electricity, water, air and feedstock. They also present reshoring opportunities to produce critical feed ingredients, such as vitamins and amino acids. Advanced fermentation technologies also offer potential in other sectors, as highlighted in the Life Sciences Strategy. All projects (if several are funded) should exploit and optimise advanced fermentation technologies with potential for the agrifood sector.

The projects are encouraged to take into account initiatives in the new EU Bioeconomy Strategy and the Horizon Europe work programme 2026-2027 in relation to industrial symbiosis, biomass hubs and biomass flows.
